entities.summary:
Marcus Pedo Vergilianus was consul at the beginning of AD 115, during the reign of Trajan. He died in an earthquake toward the end of that year. His true family name is uncertain, his gens being omitted from surviving versions of his name.
















Marcus Pedo Vergilianus was a member of the Roman aristocracy and a prominent figure in the Roman Senate. He played a significant role in the governance of the Roman Empire during the late 1st century AD. His death in the earthquake of AD 115 had a significant impact on the Roman Empire, as it led to a power struggle between different factions in the Senate.

















The earthquake of AD 115 also had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Empire. It led to a period of instability and power struggles, which ultimately resulted in the rise of a new dynasty. The legacy of Marcus Pedo Vergilianus can be seen in the continued influence of the Roman Empire on Western civilization.

















In conclusion, Marcus Pedo Vergilianus was a significant figure in Roman history, whose death in the earthquake of AD 115 had a lasting impact on the Roman Empire and Western civilization. His legacy continues to be felt today, and he remains an important figure in the study of Roman history.
